summary: This bill amends 18 U.S.C. § 207 to bar any former federal prosecutor, for one year after leaving office, from representing or assisting a business entity in a federal prosecution or deferred prosecution agreement if the attorney personally and substantially participated in that matter while in government.

scores.thoughts: The bill amends ethics rules for former DOJ attorneys regarding post-employment representation of business entities in prosecutions or deferred prosecution agreements. It contains no provisions related to federal budgets, appropriations, or expenditures.
The bill focuses exclusively on post-employment restrictions for U.S. attorneys and makes no reference to tax policy, rates, or enforcement.
No provisions address healthcare delivery, insurance, public programs, or market structures.

The bill imposes a one-year post-employment restriction on former U.S. attorneys who participated in prosecutions or deferred prosecution agreements involving business entities. This is a narrow ethics reform aimed at reducing conflicts of interest in the federal criminal justice system, providing a tangential connection to criminal justice integrity but not addressing sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation directly.
